paragraphs.title: The Nations Fear and Rely on Their Idols

easy.explanation: The LORD calls the isles and peoples to come near and speak before him.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD call to keep silence and come near to judgment?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The isles saw it, and feared; the ends of the earth were afraid.”
easy.q: How did the isles and the ends of the earth react?

answers: They helped their neighbours and said, “Be of good courage”
They asked one another for water
easy.explanation: The people helped each other and encouraged their brothers.
easy.q: How did the people encourage one another?

answers: They were afraid because of what they saw
They wanted to leave the earth
medium.explanation: Their fear is described before they strengthen and encourage one another.
medium.q: Why did the people encourage one another?

medium.explanation: In this context, the isles are distant lands summoned before the LORD.
medium.q: In verse 1, what does “isles” most nearly mean?

answers: The people fear, encourage one another, and make an idol
The people search for water, fight, and celebrate
The people build a temple, sing, and depart
medium.explanation: The nations fear, encourage one another, and then the craftsmen strengthen an idol with tools and nails.
medium.q: What sequence is described in verses 5–7?

answers: They try to create a source of security for themselves
They are preparing a place to water the desert
They are building a house for the LORD
challenge.explanation: The craftsmen fasten the idol so that it will not move, showing reliance on human-made security.
challenge.q: What does the use of tools and nails reveal about the nations’ response?

answers: The LORD calls them to judgment, but they try to protect themselves with idols
The LORD asks for water, but they plant trees
The LORD praises the nations, but they praise Israel
challenge.explanation: The LORD summons them to answer before him, while they respond with fear and idol-making.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the LORD’s invitation and the nations’ response?

answers: The craftsmen are trying to keep it from falling or shifting
challenge.explanation: The idol must be fastened with nails because it cannot stand securely by itself.
challenge.q: What does “that it should not be moved” imply about the idol?

short_answers.question: What did the carpenter and the goldsmith do?
short_answers.answer: They encouraged one another while making and fastening the idol.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 7 describes the craftsmen strengthening one another and securing the idol with nails.

short_answers.question: What did the people say to their brothers?
short_answers.explanation: This is the encouragement recorded in verse 6.

short_answers.question: What did the LORD invite the nations to do?

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Election and the Promise of Help

answers: As the enemy of the desert
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Thou, Israel, art my servant.”
easy.q: How does the LORD describe Israel?

easy.explanation: Israel is called “the seed of Abraham my friend.”
The LORD tells Israel not to fear because he is with them and will help them.
easy.q: What command does the LORD repeatedly give Israel?

answers: The LORD is with him, strengthens him, helps him, and upholds him
medium.explanation: The LORD promises, “I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee.”
medium.q: Why does Israel not need to fear?

answers: The farthest regions from which Israel was taken
medium.explanation: The verse says that the LORD took Israel from the ends of the earth and called him.
medium.q: In verse 9, what does “the ends of the earth” refer to?

answers: Because the LORD chose Israel and did not cast him away, he promises to help him
Because Israel made idols, the LORD praises him
Because Israel found water, the LORD sends enemies
medium.explanation: The LORD says he chose Israel and did not cast him away, then promises strength and support.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between election and help?

answers: As the LORD’s servant, chosen Jacob, and Abraham’s seed
challenge.explanation: Verses 8–9 identify Israel as the LORD’s servant, Jacob whom he chose, and Abraham’s seed.
challenge.q: How is Israel’s identity described through several names?

answers: A command to build an idol
challenge.explanation: Holding Israel’s right hand accompanies the promise, “Fear not; I will help thee.”
challenge.q: What does the LORD holding Israel’s right hand symbolize?

answers: They will become strong and prevail
They will be as nothing and perish
They will receive water in the desert
challenge.explanation: The LORD says Israel’s enemies shall be ashamed, confounded, and as nothing.
challenge.q: What will happen to those who fight against Israel?

short_answers.question: Whom does the LORD call his friend?
short_answers.explanation: Israel is called “the seed of Abraham my friend.”

short_answers.question: What does the LORD promise to do with his right hand?
short_answers.answer: To uphold Israel with the right hand of his righteousness.

short_answers.question: What title is given to the LORD in verse 14?
short_answers.answer: The Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
short_answers.explanation: The LORD identifies himself as Israel’s Redeemer and Holy One.

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Victory and the Renewal of the Desert

answers: A new sharp threshing instrument with teeth
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth.”
easy.q: What does the LORD make Israel?

answers: Israel will thresh them and make the hills like chaff
easy.explanation: Israel will thresh the mountains and make the hills as chaff.
easy.q: What will happen to the mountains and hills?

answers: He will hear them and not forsake them
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I the LORD will hear them…will not forsake them.”
easy.q: What does the LORD promise the poor and needy who seek water?

answers: A tool used to separate grain or break material
medium.explanation: The image is of a sharp agricultural tool used for threshing.

answers: The wind carries them away and the whirlwind scatters them
medium.explanation: The LORD says, “the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them.”
medium.q: What happens to Israel’s enemies after they are overcome?

answers: So people may recognize that the LORD has done it
medium.explanation: The purpose is that people may see, know, consider, and understand that the LORD has done it.
medium.q: Why does the LORD provide rivers, trees, and springs in the wilderness?

answers: The LORD transforms the weak into an effective power against enemies
Israel remains weak and does nothing
The instrument is used only to water the desert
challenge.explanation: Although Israel is called a worm, the LORD makes him like a sharp threshing instrument.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between Israel’s weakness and the image of a sharp threshing instrument?

answers: Israel is strengthened, enemies are scattered, and the desert receives water and plants
Idols are built, the people fear, and the rivers dry up
Israel leaves the land, fights, and builds a city
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from Israel’s victory to the renewal of the wilderness.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence in verses 15–20?

answers: The victory leads to praise and recognition of the Holy One of Israel
Israel rejoices because he became an idol
Israel rejoices because he received no help
challenge.explanation: Israel is told to rejoice in the LORD and glory in the Holy One of Israel.
challenge.q: What does Israel’s rejoicing in the LORD show after the victory?

short_answers.question: What will the wind do to Israel’s enemies?
short_answers.answer: It will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them.

short_answers.question: Name one kind of tree the LORD promises to plant in the wilderness.
short_answers.answer: Any one of: cedar, shittah tree, myrtle, oil tree, fir tree, pine, or box tree.
short_answers.explanation: Verses 19–20 list several trees planted in the wilderness and desert.

short_answers.question: Why will the LORD provide water and trees?
short_answers.answer: So people will know that the hand of the LORD has done it.
short_answers.explanation: The signs are intended to reveal the LORD’s creative work.

paragraphs.title: The Challenge to the Idols and Their Prophecy

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Produce your cause…bring forth your strong reasons.”
easy.q: What does the LORD command the nations to bring forth?

answers: The former things and things to come
easy.explanation: The idols are challenged to declare the former things and things that are to come.
easy.q: What are the idols challenged to show?

easy.explanation: The LORD declares, “ye are of nothing, and your work of nought.”
easy.q: How are the idols and their works described at the end of the section?

answers: Arguments or proofs supporting their claims
medium.explanation: The LORD challenges the nations to present evidence for their claims.
medium.q: What does “strong reasons” mean in this passage?

answers: The ability to explain the past and reveal the future
The ability to water the desert
medium.explanation: They are told to show what has happened and what will happen.
medium.q: What ability are the idols required to demonstrate?

answers: They cannot provide reliable knowledge or an answer
medium.explanation: The passage presents no idol as able to declare, show, or answer.
medium.q: What is the result of the test placed before the idols?

answers: It would prove that they truly possessed divine knowledge
It would prove that they made the images
It would show that they could find water
challenge.explanation: The LORD says that if they could declare these things, they would be recognized as gods.
challenge.q: Why is knowledge of the past and future used as a test of the idols?

answers: They cannot speak, declare, hear, or give a dependable answer
challenge.explanation: The challenge exposes their inability to communicate or reveal knowledge.
challenge.q: What do the repeated questions emphasize about the idols?

answers: The LORD challenges the idols to prove themselves, and they are shown to be nothing
The LORD asks them for water, and they water the desert
The LORD praises them, and they conquer Israel
challenge.explanation: The challenge ends with the idols’ works exposed as nothing and worthless.
challenge.q: How do the opening and ending of the section relate?

short_answers.question: What are the idols asked to show about the future?
short_answers.answer: What shall happen and what is to come hereafter.
short_answers.explanation: The LORD challenges them to declare future events.

short_answers.question: What does “do good, or do evil” test?
short_answers.answer: Whether the idols can perform an act that would prove their power.
short_answers.explanation: The challenge asks them to act so that their power might be recognized.

short_answers.question: What does the LORD call the work of the idols?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 24 declares that their work is “of nought.”

paragraphs.title: The Redeemer, the Herald, and the Emptiness of Idols

answers: From the north and from the rising of the sun
From the sea and the desert
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I have raised up one from the north” and “from the rising of the sun.”
easy.q: From which directions does the LORD raise up the coming ruler?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will give to Jerusalem one that bringeth good tidings.”
easy.q: To whom does the LORD give one who brings good tidings?

easy.explanation: The final verse calls their molten images “wind and confusion.”
easy.q: How are the molten images described at the end of the chapter?

medium.explanation: The passage says the coming one will come upon princes as upon mortar.
medium.q: In verse 25, what does “princes” refer to?

answers: Jerusalem receives good tidings, while no reliable speaker is found among the nations
Jerusalem builds idols, while the nations bring good tidings
Jerusalem is thirsty, while the nations water it
medium.explanation: Jerusalem receives a messenger of good news, but no one among the idols can declare the future.
medium.q: What contrast is shown between Jerusalem and the nations?

answers: They cannot prove that they know the future
medium.explanation: The passage answers that there is none who declares or hears their words.
medium.q: What does the question “Who hath declared from the beginning?” imply about the idols?

answers: The LORD acts in history and gives a message, while the idols cannot declare anything
The idols give the message while the LORD is silent
The redeemer is one of the images
challenge.explanation: The LORD presents concrete action and proclamation in contrast to the silence of the idols.
challenge.q: How do the redeemer and the good tidings demonstrate the LORD’s superiority over idols?

answers: No idol or counsellor could answer the LORD’s question
There were many counsellors among the idols
All the nations had already arrived in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The LORD found no man and no counsellor able to answer a word.
challenge.q: What does “I beheld, and there was no man” suggest?

answers: The LORD raises a ruler and gives good tidings, while the idols and their works are empty
The nations successfully prophesy and the LORD fails
The desert becomes a forest through the power of idols
challenge.explanation: The section contrasts the LORD’s active and reliable proclamation with the vanity of idols.
challenge.q: What is the message of verses 25–29 as a whole?

short_answers.question: What does Jerusalem receive?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD promises a messenger of good news to Jerusalem.

short_answers.question: What could no counsellor among the idols do?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 28 says there was no counsellor who could answer.

short_answers.question: What are the works of the idols?
short_answers.explanation: The final verse says, “their works are nothing.”
